featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently attended a wedding at Kora Kendar, and while the overall ambience was pleasant, I was disappointed with the lack of proper washroom facilities. Having previously visited for a garba event a few years ago, I expected improvements in this area, but unfortunately, it was still a major inconvenience.

The venue relies on portable restrooms, commonly known as porta-potties, which are known for their discomfort and lack of cleanliness. This arrangement was highly inconvenient, especially during a wedding where guests require comfortable and hygienic washroom facilities. The absence of proper washroom amenities significantly affected the overall experience.

However, it's worth noting that Kora Kendar does excel in terms of ambiance. The atmosphere created for the event was enjoyable, and the management seemed to have put effort into creating a pleasant environment for the guests. The overall decor and arrangements were satisfactory, contributing to the positive aspects of the venue.

Despite the shortcomings in washroom facilities, Kora Kendar may still be a suitable choice for events like garba or weddings, provided that alternative arrangements are made for washroom facilities. It would greatly enhance the overall experience and ensure the comfort of guests.

featured_reviews.name: Aditi Prabhu
featured_reviews.review_text:
Ambiance: Simple, soothing, with both indoor and outdoor sitting. Located at Babhai Naka, Borivali.

Our experience: We went in for dinner on a weekday. The place was largely empty and quiet. Took them 20 mins to take our first order despite having only 4 tables being served including ours.

We ordered the following dishes:
• Bombil Fry: The coating was way too thicker and the bombil hardly present. Could barely taste the bombil.
• Prawn koliwada: Again the coating overpowered the flavor of prawns.
• Bangda Thali and Ravas thali: Both thalis were exactly the same with the same fish curry, a tiny serving of prawn preparation, another tiny serving of matki usal in one thali and another random gravy in the bangda thalis. We weren't asked about our preferences for wada, chapati or bhakri. So one thali came with wadas, the other with chapati and on placing the order the third, we were asked about our preference for chapati or bhakri then informed bhakri is probabaly over. So we okayed chapati but were served wadas.

We also ordered another plate of extra chapati which they didnt have and offered wadas but none reached our table even after 2 reminders.

Finally we finished our meals and then asked for the bill which had the extra cost of wadas which we ordered and never recieved and also for the wada in thali which we weren't informed were charged extra but were given as they didnt have chapatis or bhakris.

They did change the bill on being informed.

We also asked for regular water which we recieved almost at the end of the meal after being reminded for the fifth time.

Service: Slow, and confused even when there were just 2-3 tables with people only.

While we understand it was end if the day and hence the food there was over and also probably that is why there were many errors & delays in service. But the overall experience and food were not upto the mark or hype.

featured_reviews.review_text: Malad Fish Market is a large, busy seafood market in Malad West, just a short walk from Malad railway station (West) on Sainath Road, and is popular for fresh, relatively low-priced sea fish. Location and access Located on Sainath Road, very close to Malad Railway Station (West); it is  2–5 minutes from the station. Timings  roughly 6:00 am onwards; morning hours are the main time when the wholesale and freshest stock comes.Locals recommend going around 6:00–7:30 am if you want the best catch and prices, especially if buying in bulk. Market layout and what you getThe market is divided into multiple sections: unloading/wholesale area on the road, a covered retail area where they also clean and cut, and open sections where you buy and then pay extra at cutting counters. You typically get a wide variety of saltwater fish like pomfret, surmai, bangda, bombil, prawns, crabs and seasonal catch, with both retail and wholesale options. featured_reviews.review_text:
One of the most impressive landmarks in Mumbai. Every time I pass through it, it feels like a different experience depending on the time of the day.

During the daytime, the sea view is absolutely stunning. You can see the vast Arabian Sea stretching endlessly on both sides, and the fresh breeze makes the drive even more refreshing. The structure of the bridge itself looks so modern and powerful against the blue sky.

But at night, the whole vibe changes completely. The bridge lights up beautifully, and the Mumbai skyline looks amazing with high-rise towers glowing in the background. The reflection of lights on the water, the illuminated cables of the bridge, and the city lights together create a breathtaking scene. It honestly feels like driving through a different version of Mumbai, more glamorous and magical.

Whether you experience it in the bright daylight or under the sparkling night skyline, Bandra–Worli Sea Link never fails to impress. It’s not just a bridge; it’s a symbol of modern Mumbai.

Beyond aesthetics, the Sea Link has significantly improved connectivity and reduced travel time, showcasing how thoughtful infrastructure can transform urban life. At night, the illuminated structure looks stunning and adds a distinct charm to Mumbai’s landscape.

Overall, the Sea Link perfectly reflects Mumbai’s spirit—bold, resilient, and forward-looking. A must-experience landmark that combines design excellence, innovation, and natural beauty in one frame. 🌊✨

featured_reviews.name: Shadab Qureshi
featured_reviews.review_text:
(Officially Rajiv Gandhi Sea Link — World-Class Infrastructure Review: Hindi + English Mix)

Bandra-Worli Sea Link is one of India’s most iconic modern bridges — a symbol of engineering excellence and a functional marvel that changed how people travel across Mumbai’s western coastline. It connects Bandra (Western Suburbs) to Worli (South Mumbai) over the Arabian Sea and was designed to reduce traffic congestion and travel time dramatically.  ￼

📏 Technical & Structural Highlights:
• Length: Approximately 5.6 km, making it one of India’s longest sea bridges.  ￼
• Lanes: 8 lanes (4 in each direction) for cars and light vehicles.  ￼
• Design: Cable-stayed main spans with concrete-steel precast segments on either side — an advanced hybrid design.  ￼
• Height: The cable-stay towers rise about 126 m (like a 40+ storey building).  ￼
• Built by Hindustan Construction Company under MSRDC direction after ~9 years of construction (2000–2009).  ￼

🕰 History & Purpose:
Planning for the sea link started decades ago to ease congestion along the old Mahim Causeway route. Over 23 traffic signals were typical between Bandra and Worli before — now the Sea Link cuts that journey from sometimes 40–60 minutes down to ~10 minutes at peak hours.  ￼

🚗 Traffic & Usage:
• The bridge handles tens of thousands of vehicles daily (recent traffic has grown ~33 % year-over-year as of 2025).  ￼
• Only cars and light vehicles are allowed — two-wheelers (bikes) are not permitted due to safety and speed considerations.  ￼
• The maximum speed limit is typically around 80 km/h, and driving beyond can be dangerous (and illegal) — incidents of supercars being reprimanded for speeding have been reported.  ￼

💰 Toll & Fees:
There’s a toll to use the bridge, and rates have increased over time (around ₹85–₹145 depending on vehicle type per one-way trip, with hikes implemented in recent years).  ￼

📍 Visitor & Local Experience:
• The Sea Link is open 24/7, and people love night drives when the city lights reflect off the water, offering breathtaking views.  ￼
• Locals often enjoy the drive for photography, sunset views, and skyline scenes.  ￼
• It’s considered one of Mumbai’s must-experience drives for both residents and visitors.  ￼

⚠️ Notes & Tips:
• No stopping or parking on the bridge — it’s meant for fast uninterrupted travel.  ￼
• Heavy traffic growth means sometimes slight delays during rush hours.  ￼

📌 Overall Verdict:
Bandra-Worli Sea Link is not just a transport route — it’s a cultural and architectural landmark of Mumbai. It blends world-class engineering, practical utility, and a beautiful scenic experience into one drive. Whether you’re a commuter or a tourist, crossing this bridge — especially at sunset or night — is truly a memorable Mumbai experience.  ￼

Engineering Marvel: The bridge is India's first sea-built cable-stayed bridge, a symbol of pride for its Indian builders, and features seismic arresters to withstand earthquakes.
Views and Photography: The illuminated bridge at night provides excellent photo opportunities.
Best Viewing Spots: To see the bridge in its entirety, visitors can head to the Sealink View on Mahim Beach or the Bandra-Worli Sea Link promenade, which offers the best vantage points.
Navigation: The bridge significantly reduces travel time for Mumbaikars and offers a convenient route.
Tolls: A toll is charged for using the bridge, with different rates for cars, buses, and commercial vehicles.

Jai Hind Lunch Home,  Pali Naka,  Bandra (west)

Jai Hind is a brightest shining star of the galaxy of coastal cuisine restaurants in Mumbai.  With the few branches spread across the city,  this branch at Bandra,  Pali Naka is their first branch.  The other one is on the Linking Road, which seems to be rather spacious and well furnished.  But as a foodie, my hunt is always for a 'Value for money'  restaurants with excellent quality and quantity and this desire of mime gets fulfilled only in humble homely restaurants.  This branch at Pali Naka has been renovated recently and has only five tables in all.  I recommend to reserve a table in the evening as its a very old and famous restaurant in the area and gets filled quite soon.

The list of dishes we ordered :

1.  Patra Ni Macchi (Basa)
2. Bombil Thali
3. Chicken Sukka Thali

Let me begin with the most yummiest first. The chicken sukka was simply top quality stuff made with supreme perfection. It was creamy with great blend of masalas and literally made us lick our fingers till the end.  The chicken pieces were one of the softest and well marinated ones I ever had.  The Bombil was crispy and crunchy on the outside and soft juicy within. The soul kadi (pink broth)  was thick and made with actual coconut milk.  The texture of the chapatis were homely and rice was soft, fresh and well cooked.

Patra Ni Macchi was steamed to ultimate perfection,  which retained the original flavour of the soft melting Basa fish.  The green stuffing on it was blend of spicy and sour.

Over all,  A must visit restaurant..
Staff is helpful

Serving the finest cakes at not too exorbitant price

Have tried cakes, pastries, puffs, and many other foodstuffs from merwans, but each time I try these guys become better and better. This time I had tried the half kg version of the strawberry ganache flavor and it was absolutely delicious.

The cake has three layers of cream with soft chocolate flavored bread as the base. The topmost layer on the cake is pure white cream and it does taste delicious. It has a small dollop of strawberry jam at the top and nice design of chocolate cream on one side over the white cream. the second layer is the strawberry cream mixed with vanilla as I tasted. you can feel the sweet strawberry taste mixed with vanilla and you can see the light pinkish color of the cream.

The third layer has pure chocolate cream and you either eat all the three one at a time or at once each way you get a unique taste and that taste of the cream melting in your mouth. All in all, this was a wonderful flavor and truly loved the taste of the cake.
